title: Randomized controlled trial for time-restricted eating in overweight and obese young adults
authors: Li-min Zhang, Zhan Liu, Jia-qi Wang, Rui-qiang Li, Jing-yi Ren, Xian Gao, Shuai-shuai Lv, Lu-yao Lia...
abstract: This study randomized overweight young adults to early, late, or no time-restricted eating for 8 weeks. Early time-restricted eating showed greater metabolic health improvements than late time-restricted eating or the control group.

authors: Niki Oldenburg, Douglas G. Mashek, Lisa Harnack, Qi Wang, Emily N. C. Manoogian, Nicholas Evanoff, D...
abstract: This study compared time-restricted eating (TRE), caloric restriction (CR), and unrestricted eating (UE) over 12 weeks. TRE did not significantly improve weight or metabolic measures compared to CR or UE, though reduced eating windows correlated with lower calorie intake and visceral fat.

title: The effects of early time restricted eating plus daily caloric restriction compared to daily caloric restriction alone on continuous glucose levels
authors: Adnin Zaman, Laura Grau, Rebecca Jeffers, Sheila Steinke, Victoria A. Catenacci, Marc‐Andre Cornier,...
abstract: This study compared early time-restricted eating plus daily caloric restriction (E-TRE+DCR) to daily caloric restriction (DCR) alone for 12 weeks. No significant differences were found in glucose profiles or insulin sensitivity between the groups, except for a greater reduction in glycemic excursion amplitude with DCR alone.

title: Time‐restricted eating did not alter insulin sensitivity or β‐cell function in adults with obesity: A randomized pilot study
authors: Anne E. Bantle, Kheng Joe Lau, Qi Wang, Samar Malaeb, Tasma Harindhanavudhi, Emily N. C. Manoogian, ...
abstract: A pilot study examined the effects of 12 weeks of time-restricted eating on insulin sensitivity and beta-cell function in adults with obesity. Time-restricted eating did not significantly alter these metabolic parameters compared to unrestricted eating.

title: Effect of Time-Restricted Eating on Weight Loss in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes
authors: Vasiliki Pavlou, Sofia Cienfuegos, Shuhao Lin, Mark Ezpeleta, Kathleen Ready, Sarah Corapi, Jackie W...
abstract: A 6-month study compared time-restricted eating (TRE) to calorie restriction (CR) in adults with type 2 diabetes. TRE resulted in greater weight loss than CR, but both interventions similarly lowered HbA1c levels.

title: Effect of time restricted eating on body weight and fasting glucose in participants with obesity: results of a randomized, controlled, virtual clinical trial
authors: Pamela M. Peeke, Frank L. Greenway, Sonja K. Billes, Dachuan Zhang, Ken Fujioka
abstract: A randomized trial tested 14:10 time-restricted eating (TRE) with a weight management program. 14:10 TRE resulted in greater weight loss and improved fasting glucose compared to 12:12 TRE.

title: Time-restricted feeding improves blood glucose and insulin sensitivity in overweight patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial
authors: Tingting Che, Cheng Yan, Dingyuan Tian, Xin Zhang, Xuejun Liu, Zhongming Wu
abstract: A randomized controlled trial investigated 10-hour time-restricted feeding in overweight type 2 diabetes patients over 12 weeks. Time-restricted feeding significantly improved blood glucose, insulin sensitivity, and weight compared to a control group.

title: Randomized controlled trial for time-restricted eating in healthy volunteers without obesity
authors: Zhibo Xie, Yuning Sun, Yuqian Ye, Dandan Hu, Hua Zhang, Zhangyuting He, Haitao Zhao, Huayu Yang, Yil...
abstract: A randomized trial compared early and mid-day time-restricted eating in healthy adults. Early time-restricted eating showed greater improvements in insulin sensitivity and other metabolic markers than mid-day time-restricted eating.

title: Design and Implementation of a Time-Restricted Eating Intervention in a Randomized, Controlled Eating Study
authors: Karen White, Beiwen Wu, Scott J. Pilla, Jeanne Charleston, May Thu Thu Maw, Lawrence J. Appel, Jeann...
abstract: A randomized controlled study designed and implemented time-restricted eating (TRE) versus usual eating patterns (UEP). The study successfully achieved its intervention goals, providing a controlled method to isolate meal timing's effect on weight.

title: Weight-neutral early time-restricted eating improves glycemic variation and time in range without changes in inflammatory markers
authors: Joanne Bruno, Jeanne M. Walker, Shabnam Nasserifar, Dhairya Upadhyay, Andrea Ronning, Sally M. Vaneg...
abstract: Early time-restricted eating was studied in adults with prediabetes. It improved glycemic control without affecting inflammatory markers.

title: Protocol for a single-centre, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial on the effects of time-restricted eating on body weight, behaviour and metabolism in individuals at high risk of type 2 diabetes: the REStricted Eating Time (RESET) study
authors: Jonas S Quist, Marie M Jensen, Kim K B Clemmensen, Hanne Pedersen, Natasja Bjerre, Joachim Størling,...
abstract: This study investigates the effects of time-restricted eating on body weight, behavior, and metabolism in individuals at high risk for type 2 diabetes. The primary outcome is change in body weight after 3 months.

title: Efficacy of Time-Restricted Eating and Behavioral Economic Intervention in Reducing Fasting Plasma Glucose, HbA1c, and Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Patients with Impaired Fasting Glucose: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Unyaporn Suthutvoravut, Thunyarat Anothaisintawee, Suparee Boonmanunt, Sarunporn Pramyothin, Sukanya...
abstract: This study compared time-restricted eating (TRE) with or without behavioral economics (BE) interventions against usual care for impaired fasting glucose patients. No significant differences were found between groups, but TRE showed benefits for those who adhered to the protocol.

title: Effects of Early vs. Late Time-Restricted Eating on Cardiometabolic Health, Inflammation, and Sleep in Overweight and Obese Women: A Study Protocol for the ChronoFast Trial
authors: Beeke Peters, Daniela A. Koppold-Liebscher, Bettina Schuppelius, Nico Steckhan, Andreas F. H. Pfeiff...
abstract: This study protocol outlines a trial comparing early versus late time-restricted eating in overweight/obese women. The trial aims to determine which eating pattern better improves cardiometabolic health, inflammation, and sleep.

title: Protocol for a 1‐year randomised, controlled, parallel group, open‐label trial on the effects and feasibility of time‐restricted eating in individuals with type 2 diabetes‐ The REStricted Eating Time in the treatment of type 2 diabetes ( RESET2 ) trial
authors: Anne‐Ditte Termannsen, Annemarie Varming, Natasja Bjerre, Helena Z. Wodschow, Gitte S. Hansen, Nicol...
abstract: This paper describes the protocol for a one-year randomized trial investigating time-restricted eating (TRE) in type 2 diabetes. The trial aims to assess TRE's effects on glycaemic control and feasibility.

title: Time restricted eating as a weight loss intervention in adults with obesity
authors: Dunja Przulj, Daniella Ladmore, Katie Myers Smith, Anna Phillips-Waller, Peter Hajek
abstract: This pilot study assessed adherence and effects of time-restricted eating (TRE) on weight and lipids in adults with obesity. TRE showed modest weight loss comparable to other interventions, with no significant impact on blood pressure or lipids.

title: The basis and design for time‐restricted eating compared with daily calorie restriction for weight loss and colorectal cancer risk reduction trial ( TRE‐CRC  trial)
authors: Kelsey Gabel, Marian L. Fitzgibbon, Cemal Yazici, Peter Gann, Maria Sverdlov, Grace Guzman, Zhengjia...
abstract: A randomized controlled trial compared 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE) with daily calorie restriction (Cal-R) and a control group in adults with obesity and increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk. The study will examine the effects of these interventions on weight, metabolic markers, and CRC risk.

title: Three weeks of time-restricted eating improves glucose homeostasis in adults with type 2 diabetes but does not improve insulin sensitivity: a randomised crossover trial
authors: Charlotte Andriessen, Ciarán E. Fealy, Anna Veelen, Sten M. M. van Beek, Kay H. M. Roumans, Niels J....
abstract: Three weeks of time-restricted eating improved glucose homeostasis in adults with type 2 diabetes. However, it did not improve insulin sensitivity.

title: Effect of Time-Restricted Eating on Circulating Levels of IGF1 and Its Binding Proteins in Obesity: An Exploratory Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Rand Talal Akasheh, Aparna Ankireddy, Kelsey Gabel, Mark Ezpeleta, Shuhao Lin, Chandra Mohan Tamatam...
abstract: This study explored the effects of 4 and 6-hour time-restricted eating (TRE) on IGF1 and its binding proteins in individuals with obesity. TRE significantly reduced body weight and improved insulin sensitivity, but did not alter IGF1 or IGFBP3 levels.

title: Time-restricted eating for patients with diabetes and prediabetes: A systematic review
authors: Xiaoxiao Lin, Yihong Guan, Guomin Wu, Jinyu Huang, Shuai Wang
abstract: A systematic review analyzed seven studies on time-restricted eating for diabetes and prediabetes. Time-restricted eating appears safe and may improve weight, insulin sensitivity, and blood glucose.

title: The impact of a self-selected time restricted eating intervention on eating patterns, sleep, and late-night eating in individuals with obesity
authors: Stacey L. Simon, Jennifer Blankenship, Emily N. C. Manoogian, Satchidananda Panda, Douglas G. Mashek...
abstract: A self-selected time-restricted eating intervention shifted meal timing and reduced late-night eating in individuals with obesity. This intervention was associated with longer sleep duration and improved eating patterns.

title: Time-Restricted Eating Alters Food Intake Patterns, as Prospectively Documented by a Smartphone Application
authors: Samar Malaeb, Tasma Harindhanavudhi, Katrina Dietsche, Nick Esch, Emily N. C. Manoogian, Satchidanan...
abstract: This study examined how time-restricted eating (TRE) affects food intake patterns using a smartphone app. TRE significantly reduced eating occasions, snacks, and caffeinated beverages compared to baseline and a control group.

title: Early Time-Restricted Eating Reduces Weight and Improves Glycemic Response in Young Adults: A Pre-Post Single-Arm Intervention Study
authors: JinA Kim, YoonJu Song
abstract: This study examined the effects of early time-restricted eating (TRE) on young adults. Early TRE, starting before noon, significantly reduced weight, fat mass, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, and triglycerides.

title: Effects of time-restricted eating with different eating windows on human metabolic health: pooled analysis of existing cohorts
authors: Zhongbiao Nie, Jiaming Xu, Yinchu Cheng, Zhihong Li, Ran Zhang, Wentao Zhang, Libo Zhao
abstract: A network meta-analysis compared time-restricted eating (TRE) with different eating windows on metabolic health. No specific eating window showed significant metabolic advantages over others, suggesting similar benefits across various TRE durations.

title: Early time-restricted eating improves markers of cardiometabolic health but has no impact on intestinal nutrient absorption in healthy adults
authors: M. Alan Dawson, Susan N. Cheung, Michael R. La Frano, Ravinder Nagpal, Claire E. Berryman
abstract: Early time-restricted eating improved cardiometabolic health markers in healthy adults. However, it did not affect intestinal nutrient absorption or gastrointestinal function.

title: Exploring Rates of Adherence and Barriers to Time-Restricted Eating
authors: Paul W. Jefcoate, M. Denise Robertson, Jane Ogden, Jonathan D. Johnston
abstract: This study assessed adherence to a 5-week time-restricted eating (TRE) protocol and identified barriers. Objective and subjective adherence was around 63%, with work, social, and family life posing challenges.

title: Time-restricted eating improves health because of energy deficit and circadian rhythm: A systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Yuwen Chang, Tingting Du, Xiangling Zhuang, Guojie Ma
abstract: This systematic review analyzed the effects of time-restricted eating (TRE) in humans with overweight or obesity. TRE resulted in modest weight loss and improved various metabolic markers, primarily due to energy deficit, with circadian alignment playing a secondary role.

title: The effects of time‐restricted eating and weight loss on bone metabolism and health: a 6‐month randomized controlled trial
authors: Maria Papageorgiou, Emmanuel Biver, Julie Mareschal, Nicholas Edward Phillips, Alexandra Hemmer, Emm...
abstract: This study compared time-restricted eating (TRE) to standard dietary advice for bone health in adults with metabolic syndrome. TRE showed bone-sparing effects compared to standard advice when weight loss occurred.

title: Time-Restricted Eating and Sleep, Mood, and Quality of Life in Adults With Overweight or Obesity
authors: Antonio Clavero-Jimeno, Manuel Dote-Montero, Jairo H. Migueles, Alba Camacho-Cardenosa, María Medran...
abstract: This study analyzed the effects of early, late, or self-selected time-restricted eating windows on sleep, mood, and quality of life in adults with overweight or obesity. No significant differences were found between any time-restricted eating patterns and usual care for these outcomes.

title: Early Time-Restricted Eating Improves Weight Loss While Preserving Muscle: An 8-Week Trial in Young Women
authors: Zifu Yu, Takeshi Ueda
abstract: An 8-week trial studied early, delayed, or no time-restricted eating in young women performing resistance training. Early time-restricted eating led to greater weight loss than delayed or no restrictions, without negatively impacting muscle gains.

title: Comparing the influence of early and late time-restricted eating with energy restriction and energy restriction alone on cardiometabolic markers, metabolic hormones and appetite in adults with overweight/obesity: per-protocol analysis of a 3-month randomized clinical trial
authors: Bernarda Habe, Tanja Črešnovar, Ana Petelin, Saša Kenig, Nina Mohorko, Zala Jenko Pražnikar
abstract: This study compared early time-restricted eating plus energy restriction (eTRE+ER) with late time-restricted eating plus energy restriction (lTRE+ER) and energy restriction alone (ER).

title: Perspective: Time-Restricted Eating—Integrating the What with the When
authors: Evelyn B Parr, Brooke L Devlin, John A Hawley
abstract: This paper reviews time-restricted eating (TRE) interventions and their impact on health outcomes. It concludes that integrating knowledge of *what* is eaten with *when* it is eaten is crucial for optimizing TRE's metabolic health benefits.

title: Effect of Time-Restricted Eating on Sleep in Type 2 Diabetes
authors: Vasiliki Pavlou, Shuhao Lin, Sofia Cienfuegos, Mark Ezpeleta, Mary-Claire Runchey, Sarah Corapi, Kel...
abstract: This study compared time-restricted eating (TRE) to calorie restriction and controls in adults with type 2 diabetes. TRE did not improve sleep quality, duration, or insomnia severity compared to the other groups.

title: The Effects of Time-Restricted Eating versus Standard Dietary Advice on Weight, Metabolic Health and the Consumption of Processed Food: A Pragmatic Randomised Controlled Trial in Community-Based Adults
authors: Nicholas Edward Phillips, Julie Mareschal, Nathalie Schwab, Emily N. C. Manoogian, Sylvie Borloz, Gi...
abstract: This study examined the link between eating habits and metabolic health, and compared time-restricted eating (TRE) to standard dietary advice. TRE showed a small but significant weight loss compared to no change with standard advice, though the difference between groups was not significant.

title: Time-restricted eating plus calorie-restricted diet versus calorie-restricted diet in women with polycystic ovary syndrome
authors: Silan Zheng, Yun Chen, Xin Zheng, Danyan Ma, Xiaohong Yan, Jiayu Zhang, Changqin Liu
abstract: This study compared an 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE) diet with a calorie-restricted diet (CRD) in women with PCOS. The TRE group achieved greater weight loss and improved insulin resistance compared to the CRD group.

title: Time-restricted eating on weight loss: implications from the TREATY study
authors: Yan Huang, Deying Liu, Xueyun Wei, Chensihan Huang, Changwei Li, Huijie Zhang

title: Effectiveness of isocaloric early time‐restricted eating on glucose metabolism in adults: A randomized controlled crossover trial
authors: Minfang Weng, Sisi Deng, Wei Xie, Yuqi Ma, Yeran Jia

title: Effects of timing and eating duration of time restricted eating on metabolic outcomes: systematic review and network meta-analysis
authors: Yu-En Chen, Hui-Li Tsai, Yu-Kang Tu, Ling-Wei Chen
abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated time-restricted eating's effects on metabolic health. Early time-restricted eating showed the most consistent benefits for anthropometric and glycaemic outcomes.

title: Time-Restricted Eating Improves Quality of Life Measures in Overweight Humans
authors: Ainslee Crose, Alison Alvear, Stephanie Singroy, Qi Wang, Emily Manoogian, Satchidananda Panda, Doug...
abstract: A randomized trial examined time-restricted eating (TRE) versus unrestricted eating in overweight individuals. TRE was associated with modest improvements in emotional health and perceived health changes.

title: Time-Restricted Eating Versus Daily Calorie Restriction: Effect on Sleep in Adults with Obesity over 12 Months
authors: Shuhao Lin, Sofia Cienfuegos, Mark Ezpeleta, Kelsey Gabel, Vasiliki Pavlou, Shaina J. Alexandria, Kr...
abstract: This study compared time-restricted eating (TRE) and daily calorie restriction (CR) on sleep in adults with obesity. Neither TRE nor CR significantly improved sleep quality, duration, insomnia, or sleep apnea risk after 12 months.

title: Early Time-Restricted Feeding Reduces Appetite and Increases Fat Oxidation but Does Not Affect Energy Expenditure in Humans
authors: Eric Ravussin, Robbie A. Beyl, Eleonora Poggiogalle, Daniel S. Hsia, Courtney M. Peterson
abstract: Early time-restricted feeding (eTRF) was studied in overweight adults. eTRF reduced appetite and increased fat oxidation without changing 24-hour energy expenditure.

authors: Iwona Świątkiewicz, Jarosław Nuszkiewicz, Joanna Wróblewska, Małgorzata Nartowicz, Kamil Sokołowski,...
abstract: A 12-week time-restricted eating (TRE) intervention was studied in Polish patients with metabolic syndrome. TRE was feasible and led to reduced eating window duration, weight, blood pressure, and improved glucose control.

title: Evaluating evidence regarding the efficacy of time-restricted eating for weight loss
authors: David E. Most

abstract: A smartphone intervention tested time-restricted eating (TRE) in adults with overweight/obesity. TRE significantly reduced body weight, waist circumference, and systolic blood pressure.

title: Effects of time-restricted eating with different eating duration on anthropometrics and cardiometabolic health: A systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Mazuin Kamarul Zaman, Nur Islami Mohd Fahmi Teng, Sazzli Shahlan Kasim, Norsham Juliana, Mohammed Ab...
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the effects of time-restricted eating (TRE) on anthropometrics and cardiometabolic health. TRE significantly reduced body weight and fat mass, but its impact varied based on the duration of the eating window.

title: Time–restricted eating alters the 24‐hour profile of adipose tissue transcriptome in men with obesity
authors: Lijun Zhao, Amy T. Hutchison, Bo Liu, Gary A. Wittert, Campbell H. Thompson, Leanne Nguyen, John Au,...
abstract: This study examined how time-restricted eating affects 24-hour profiles of hormones, metabolites, and adipose tissue gene expression in men with obesity. Time-restricted eating restored rhythmic patterns in these factors, suggesting a mechanism for improved metabolic health.

title: A Delayed Morning and Earlier Evening Time-Restricted Feeding Protocol for Improving Glycemic Control and Dietary Adherence in Men with Overweight/Obesity: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Evelyn B. Parr, Brooke L. Devlin, Bridget E. Radford, John A. Hawley
abstract: A randomized controlled trial compared time-restricted feeding (TRF) with extended feeding in overweight/obese men. TRF improved nocturnal glycemic control and was positively perceived, despite some adherence challenges.

title: Time-restricted feeding: what we have done and what more we can do?
authors: Yuning Sun, Yuqian Ye, Yuqin He, Shaoyan Liu

title: Effects of sleep restriction on glucose control and insulin secretion during diet-induced weight loss
authors: A. V. Nedeltcheva, J. G. Imperial, P. D. Penev
abstract: This study investigated the effects of sleep restriction on glucose control in overweight adults undergoing weight loss. Sleep restriction enhanced insulin economy without negatively impacting glucose homeostasis during dieting.

title: Time restricted EAting for Type 2 diabetes and MEtabolic health: The TEA TIME trial study protocol
authors: Matthew Retnakaran; Vittória L. Lessa; Caroline K. Kramer
abstract: This study protocol outlines a one-year randomized controlled trial to assess the durability of time-restricted eating (TRE) in improving metabolic health for individuals with type 2 diabetes. The trial will compare TRE (6-hour eating window daily) against standard recommendations, measuring pancreatic beta-cell function and insulin resistance over 52 weeks. Findings could establish TRE as a disease-modifying intervention for early type 2 diabetes.

title: Pilot Clinical Trial of Time-Restricted Eating in Patients with Metabolic Syndrome
authors: Iwona Świątkiewicz, Celestyna Mila-Kierzenkowska, Alina Woźniak, Karolina Szewczyk-Golec, Jarosław N...
abstract: This pilot trial investigated the feasibility and efficacy of 10-hour time-restricted eating in Polish adults with metabolic syndrome. The study aims to establish a framework for future large-scale trials by assessing cardiometabolic outcomes and behavioral rhythms.

title: Time-Restricted Eating: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Challenges in Translation
authors: Prashant Regmi, Leonie K. Heilbronn
abstract: This paper reviews time-restricted eating (TRE), a dietary approach that limits eating to a specific window each day. TRE demonstrates significant benefits for metabolic health, including weight loss and improved glucose tolerance, though implementation challenges exist.

title: Time Restricted Eating: A Dietary Strategy to Prevent and Treat Metabolic Disturbances
authors: Bettina Schuppelius, Beeke Peters, Agnieszka Ottawa, Olga Pivovarova-Ramich
abstract: This review examines how time-restricted eating affects glucose and lipid metabolism based on clinical trials. TRE shows promise for improving metabolic health, though results vary due to study design and participant differences.

title: Efficacy of time-restricted eating and behavioural economic interventions in reducing fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c and cardiometabolic risk factors compared with time-restricted eating alone or usual care in patients with impaired fasting glucose: protocol for an open-label randomised controlled trial
authors: Unyaporn Suthutvoravut, Thunyarat Anothaisintawee, Suparee Boonmanunt, Sarunporn Pramyothin, Arthit ...
abstract: This study will compare time-restricted eating (TRE) with behavioral economic interventions, TRE alone, and usual care in patients with impaired fasting glucose. The goal is to determine if TRE, especially with added behavioral support, improves cardiometabolic risk factors.

title: Early Time-Restricted Feeding Improves 24-Hour Glucose Levels and Affects Markers of the Circadian Clock, Aging, and Autophagy in Humans
authors: Humaira Jamshed, Robbie A. Beyl, Deborah L. Della Manna, Eddy S. Yang, Eric Ravussin, Courtney M. Pe...
abstract: Early time-restricted feeding was studied in overweight adults. It improved 24-hour glucose levels and altered circadian clock, aging, and autophagy markers.

title: Exploring the effects of time-restricted eating on body weight and associated cardiometabolic outcomes in South African women living with HIV (TESSA): protocol for a randomised controlled trial
authors: Amy E Mendham, Julia H Goedecke, Lorena Heckens, Fatima Hoosen, Majken Lillholm Pico, Andre P Kengne...
abstract: This study investigates the effects of time-restricted eating on body weight and cardiometabolic outcomes in South African women with HIV. The trial aims to determine if TRE improves these health markers over 12 months.

authors: Xiaoyan Shi, Peien Jiang, Penghao Wang, Xingwei Guo, Mengxuan Ye, Zhiying Jiang, Yan Chen, Tingjuan ...
abstract: A randomized trial will compare 12-hour time-restricted eating (TRE) to caloric-restricted diets for weight loss in obese children. The study aims to determine TRE's short-term and long-term efficacy and adherence compared to standard treatment.

authors: Robert Jones, Pardeep Pabla, Joanne Mallinson, Aline Nixon, Tariq Taylor, Andrew Bennett, Kostas Tsi...
abstract: Two weeks of early time-restricted feeding was studied in healthy men. This intervention improved whole-body insulin sensitivity and skeletal muscle glucose and amino acid uptake.

title: The Effect of Time-Restricted Eating on Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Krystalia Panagiotou, Garyfallia Stefanou, Georgia Kourlaba, Dimitrios Athanasopoulos, Penio Kassari...
abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis examined the effects of time-restricted eating (TRE) on cardiometabolic risk factors. TRE was found to be beneficial for weight loss and improving insulin, cholesterol, and LDL levels.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Adolescents With Obesity: Monitoring of Glucose Profiles, Glycemic Excursions, and Adherence to Time Restricted Eating Programs
authors: Monica N. Naguib, Elizabeth Hegedus, Jennifer K. Raymond, Michael I. Goran, Sarah-Jeanne Salvy, Choo...
abstract: This study assessed continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) feasibility and glycemic profiles in adolescents with obesity undergoing a time-restricted eating (TRE) pilot trial. CGM use was feasible and acceptable, but TRE did not significantly alter glycemic variability compared to a control group.

authors: Michael J. Wilkinson; Erika Padilla; Yuqi Wang; Sawye Raygani; Emily N. C. Manoogian; Kyla Laing; Kh...
abstract: Examine time‐restricted eating (TRE) as a strategy to promote weight loss and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity. TRE in obesity and ADipose Tissue (TREAD) was a single‐center 12‐week RCT,

authors: Elizabeth Z. Gipson; G. Chretienne Kang; Katelynn E. Hales; Dallin J. Kemp; Dane T. Jensen; Lance E....
abstract: Initiating a 24-hour fast in the afternoon, rather than morning or evening, resulted in better glycemic control and increased ketosis. These improvements were observed throughout the fast and after refeeding, independent of insulin and glucagon levels.

title: Health effects of the time-restricted eating in adults with obesity: A systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Weiyi Chen, Xiaoli Liu, Lei Bao, Ping Yang, Huihui Zhou
abstract: This study systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed randomized controlled trials on time-restricted eating (TRE) in adults with obesity. TRE was found to significantly decrease body weight, fat mass, BMI, and diastolic blood pressure.

title: Is  time‐restricted  eating (8/16) beneficial for body weight and metabolism of obese and overweight adults? A systematic review and meta‐analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Lu Huang, Yan Chen, Shu Wen, Danhua Lu, Xiaoyang Shen, Hongxia Deng, Liangzhi Xu
abstract: This meta-analysis examined randomized controlled trials on 8/16 time-restricted eating in overweight and obese adults. The intervention led to significant reductions in body weight and fat mass, and improved insulin resistance.

title: Effects of time-restricted eating without caloric restriction on blood pressure and cardiometabolic profile in non-diabetic adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated time-restricted eating (TRE) without caloric restriction in non-diabetic adults. TRE significantly reduced blood pressure, heart rate, glucose, insulin, and BMI, but not lipid profiles.

title: A randomized feasibility trial of time-restricted eating during pregnancy in people with increased risk of gestational diabetes
authors: Hanna M.S. Skarstad, Kamilla L. Haganes, Md Abu Jafar Sujan, Trine M. Gellein, Mariell K. Johansen, ...
abstract: A randomized trial tested a 10-hour time-restricted eating window for pregnant individuals at risk of gestational diabetes. The intervention was feasible but did not improve glycemic control or other cardiometabolic outcomes.

authors: Rhonda M. Merwin, Natalia O. Dmitrieva, Lisa K. Honeycutt, Ashley A. Moskovich, James D. Lane, Nancy...
abstract: This study examined momentary predictors of insulin restriction in adults with type 1 diabetes and eating disorder symptomatology. Heightened negative affect and breaking dietary rules predicted insulin restriction.

title: Effect of a ketogenic diet, time-restricted eating, or alternate-day fasting on weight loss in adults with obesity: a randomized clinical trial
authors: José Ignacio Martínez-Montoro, Borja Bandera, Mario Gutiérrez-Bedmar, Ana María Gómez-Pérez, Manuel ...
abstract: A randomized trial compared calorie-restricted ketogenic diets, time-restricted eating, and alternate-day fasting to a Mediterranean diet for weight loss in adults with obesity. title: Effects of 8-hour time restricted feeding on body weight and metabolic disease risk factors in obese adults: A pilot study
authors: Kelsey Gabel, Kristin K. Hoddy, Nicole Haggerty, Jeehee Song, Cynthia M. Kroeger, John F. Trepanowsk...
abstract: This pilot study examined the effects of 8-hour time-restricted feeding on obese adults over 12 weeks. The intervention led to mild weight loss and a reduction in systolic blood pressure compared to a control group.

title: The Effect of Early Time-Restricted Feeding on Glycemic Profile in Adults: A Systematic Review of Interventional Studies
authors: Demetrios Bitsanis, Konstantinos Giannakou, Elena Hadjimbei, Stavri Chrysostomou
abstract: This systematic review analyzed interventional studies on early time-restricted feeding (eTRF) and its impact on adult glycemic profiles. eTRF appears to positively affect glucose and insulin markers, particularly in healthy individuals with normal BMI.

authors: Leonie C. Ruddick-Collins, Peter J. Morgan, Claire L. Fyfe, Joao A.N. Filipe, Graham W. Horgan, Klaa...
abstract: A study compared morning-loaded versus evening-loaded calorie-restricted diets in individuals with obesity. While weight loss and energy expenditure were similar, the morning-loaded diet significantly reduced hunger, suggesting it may improve adherence to weight loss plans.

abstract: Rising obesity rates necessitate sustainable weight management strategies. Current lifestyle guidelines focus on reducing caloric intake through personalized interventions to promote compliance. This

authors: Marriam Ali, Sirimon Reutrakul, Gregory Petersen, Kristen L. Knutson
abstract: This study examined the association between eating timing and duration with glucose metabolism in a U.S. population. Earlier eating start times were linked to lower fasting glucose and insulin resistance, independent of eating duration.

title: Association between Timing of Energy Intake and Insulin Sensitivity: A Cross-Sectional Study
authors: Vittobai Rashika Rangaraj, Alankrita Siddula, Helen J. Burgess, Silvana Pannain, Kristen L. Knutson
abstract: This study examined the relationship between when people eat and their insulin sensitivity. Eating more calories earlier in the day was linked to better insulin sensitivity.

title: Effects of Time-Restricted Eating on Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
authors: Xueyun Wei, Bingquan Lin, Yan Huang, Shunyu Yang, Chensihan Huang, Linna Shi, Deying Liu, Peizhen Zh...
abstract: A randomized trial compared time-restricted eating to daily calorie restriction for nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. Both interventions similarly reduced liver fat, with no added benefits from time-restricted eating.

title: Early but not late time-restricted eating improves an actigraphy-estimated sleep quality in women with overweight or obesity: secondary analysis of the crossover ChronoFast trial
authors: Beeke Peters; Jennifer Jokisch; Julia Schwarz; Bettina Schuppelius; Andreas F. H. Pfeiffer; Andreas ...
abstract: Metabolic disorders are closely linked to sleep disturbances. Time-restricted eating (TRE) can improve metabolic disturbances, but its impact on sleep quality is insufficiently studied and recommendat

title: The effect of time-restricted eating on arterial stiffness indices in men with metabolic syndrome: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
authors: Aliyeh Ghannadzadeh Yazdi, Mohammad Masoumvand, Elena Philippou, Alireza Hatami, Zahra Dehnavi, Hani...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial protocol outlines a study comparing time-restricted eating to standard dietary advice for men with metabolic syndrome. The study aims to determine the effect of time-restricted eating on arterial stiffness indices.

title: Time-Restricted Eating as a Nutrition Strategy for Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Feasibility Study
authors: Evelyn B. Parr, Brooke L. Devlin, Karen H. C. Lim, Laura N. Z. Moresi, Claudia Geils, Leah Brennan, ...
abstract: This study assessed the feasibility of time-restricted eating (TRE) for individuals with type 2 diabetes. TRE was found to be feasible, with participants adhering to the eating window approximately five days a week, though it did not significantly improve glycemic control or reduce body mass.

title: Time-Restricted Feeding Improves Glucose Tolerance in Rats, but Only When in Line With the Circadian Timing System
authors: Paul de Goede, Ewout Foppen, Wayne I. G. R. Ritsema, Nikita L. Korpel, Chun-Xia Yi, Andries Kalsbeek
abstract: Time-restricted feeding (TRF) in rats was studied to assess its impact on glucose tolerance across different times of day. TRF aligned with the active phase improved glucose tolerance, while feeding out of sync worsened it.

title: Effect of exercise alone and in combination with time-restricted eating on cardiometabolic health in menopausal women
authors: Beata Jóźwiak, Remigiusz Domin, Monika Krzywicka, Ida Laudańska-Krzemińska
abstract: This study compared exercise alone versus exercise with time-restricted eating in menopausal women. Combining time-restricted eating with exercise resulted in greater reductions in body mass index and blood pressure than exercise alone.

title: Effect of time-restricted eating regimen on weight loss is mediated by gut microbiome
authors: Chensihan Huang, Deying Liu, Shunyu Yang, Yan Huang, Xueyun Wei, Peizhen Zhang, Jiayang Lin, Bingyan...
abstract: This study investigated the gut microbiome's role in weight loss during a 12-month time-restricted eating program. The gut microbiome composition at baseline can predict an individual's weight loss response to TRE.

title: Effects of Time-Restricted Feeding on Energy Balance: A Cross-Over Trial in Healthy Subjects
authors: Riqiang Bao, Yingkai Sun, Yiran Jiang, Lei Ye, Jie Hong, Weiqing Wang
abstract: This study investigated the effects of time-restricted feeding (TRF) on energy balance in healthy individuals. TRF was found to induce a negative energy balance by increasing fecal and urine energy loss, without altering energy expenditure.

title: Bibliometric and visual analysis of time-restricted eating
authors: Shuai Wang, Xiaoxiao Lin, Yihong Guan, Jinyu Huang
abstract: This study analyzed 414 publications on time-restricted eating (TRE) using bibliometric methods. The research shows TRE is a growing field, with key themes including circadian rhythms, obesity, weight loss, and metabolic disease.

title: Effect of Early Time-Restricted Eating on Metabolic Markers and Body Composition in Individuals with Overweight or Obesity
authors: Dalila Rubí Mena-Hernández, Guadalupe Jiménez-Domínguez, José D. Méndez, Viridiana Olvera-Hernández,...
abstract: This study investigated early time-restricted eating (eTRE) in overweight or obese individuals. eTRE did not significantly improve metabolic markers, body composition, or appetite compared to a control group.

title: Early time-restricted carbohydrate consumption vs conventional dieting in type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial
authors: Domenico Tricò, Maria Chiara Masoni, Simona Baldi, Noemi Cimbalo, Luca Sacchetta, Maria Tiziana Scoz...
abstract: This study compared early time-restricted carbohydrate consumption with a conventional diet in individuals with type 2 diabetes. Both diets resulted in similar improvements in HbA1c, glucose control, and cardiometabolic markers.

title: Improvement and Emergence of Insulin Restriction in Women With Type 1 Diabetes
authors: Ann E. Goebel-Fabbri, Barbara J. Anderson, Janna Fikkan, Debra L. Franko, Kimberly Pearson, Katie We...
abstract: This study examined characteristics of women with type 1 diabetes who stopped or started insulin restriction over 11 years. Fear of weight gain and diabetes self-care problems are central to both the development and cessation of insulin restriction.

title: Effects of Early and Late Time-Restricted Feeding on Parameters of Metabolic Health: An Explorative Literature Assessment
authors: Froso Petridi, Jan M. W. Geurts, Jean Nyakayiru, Anne Schaafsma, Dedmer Schaafsma, Ruth C. R. Meex, ...
abstract: This literature assessment examined 13 trials on early and late time-restricted feeding's effects on metabolic health. Time-restricted feeding consistently reduced body weight and improved insulin resistance, with early feeding showing a potentially greater benefit for insulin resistance.

title: Navigating challenges and adherence in time‐restricted eating: A qualitative study
authors: Hilmi S. Rathomi, Nahal Mavaddat, Judith M. Katzenellenbogen, Sandra C. Thompson
abstract: This study explored facilitators, barriers, and strategies for adherence to time-restricted eating. Key findings indicate that flexibility, a non-obsessive mindset, and social support facilitate adherence, while hunger and social conflicts pose challenges.

title: Time-restricted eating and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a pilot, randomized clinical trial
authors: Cortney Steele, Anna Ostrow, Wei Wang, Erin Coleman, Diana George, Kristen Bing, Sumana Ramanathan, ...
abstract: A pilot randomized trial compared time-restricted eating (TRE) with healthy eating advice for ADPKD patients. TRE did not significantly reduce kidney volume, and adherence was moderate, suggesting weight and adiposity loss may be more critical.

title: Time-restricted eating in Alzheimer's disease: TREAD pilot trial design
authors: Susan B. Racette, Jordan A. Gunning, Danielle E. Eagan, Isabella Zaniletti, Tracy L. Smith, Candice ...
abstract: The TREAD pilot trial is evaluating the feasibility of a 16-hour fasting, 8-hour eating window intervention for individuals with mild cognitive impairment. It will collect preliminary data on cognitive function and biomarkers to inform future larger studies.

title: Time-Restricted Eating and Its Metabolic Benefits
authors: Sneha Mishra, Patress A. Persons, Andrea M. Lorenzo, Swarna S. Chaliki, Sophie Bersoux
abstract: This paper reviews time-restricted eating (TRE) and its metabolic effects. TRE is found to be equivalent to calorie restriction for weight loss and beneficial for various diseases.

title: Take the reins: a study protocol of a randomized controlled trial testing the effects of time-restricted eating vs. nutrition control on cancer-related fatigue among survivors of hematological malignancies
authors: Amber S. Kleckner, Carin L. Clingan, Ashraf Z. Badros, Emily N. C. Manoogian, Karen M. Mustian, Satc...
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial comparing time-restricted eating to nutrition counseling for cancer-related fatigue in blood cancer survivors. The intervention aims to improve fatigue by regulating circadian rhythms and metabolism.

title: Meal Timing Interventions for Weight Loss and Metabolic Health—What Does the Evidence Tell Us So Far?
authors: Collin J. Popp, Emily N. C. Manoogian, Blandine Laferrère

title: Effects of time-restricted eating on body composition and metabolic parameters in overweight and obese women: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Shiying Chen, Xiaotian Zhang, Jakub Kortas, Haitao Liu
abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated time-restricted eating (TRE) in overweight and obese women. TRE significantly reduced body weight and fasting insulin levels, with no adverse effects on lean mass.

title: Predicting the restrictive eating, exercise, and weight monitoring compulsions of anorexia nervosa
authors: E. Caitlin Lloyd, Maria Øverås, Øyvind Rø, Bas Verplanken, Anne M. Haase
abstract: This study compared restrictive eating, exercise, and weight monitoring compulsions in individuals with anorexia nervosa (AN) and healthy controls. Neither AN psychopathology nor trait anxiety predicted the presence of these compulsions, though the study was likely underpowered.

title: Effects of healthy low-carbohydrate diet and time-restricted eating on weight and gut microbiome in adults with overweight or obesity: Feeding RCT
authors: Lin Li, Rui Li, Qingying Tian, Yaogan Luo, Ruyi Li, Xiaoyu Lin, Yunjing Ou, Tianyu Guo, Xue Chen, An...
abstract: A randomized trial investigated healthy low-carbohydrate diet (HLCD) and time-restricted eating (TRE) effects on weight and gut microbiome. Both HLCD and TRE reduced BMI beyond calorie restriction, with HLCD also reducing fat mass and TRE increasing beneficial gut bacteria.

title: Effect of Time‐Restricted Eating on Metabolic Adaptation in Adults With Severe Obesity During Early Phase of Weight Loss
authors: Tatiana Almeida de Moraes Campos; Raiane Lira Freitas Brasil; Flávia Fioruci Bezerra
source: Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics
abstract: To compare metabolic adaptations at the early phase of weight loss in individuals with severe obesity assigned to two strategies of energy restriction: continuous or in combination with time‐restricte

title: Twenty-Four Hour Glucose Profiles and Glycemic Variability during Intermittent Religious Dry Fasting and Time-Restricted Eating in Subjects without Diabetes: A Preliminary Study
authors: Beeke Peters, Christina Laetitia Pappe, Daniela A. Koppold, Katharina Schipp, Bert Arnrich, Andreas ...
abstract: This study examined 24-hour glucose profiles and variability in non-diabetic individuals undergoing religious fasting or time-restricted eating. Both fasting and time-restricted eating did not negatively impact glycemic control or variability.

title: Effects of intermittent (5:2) or continuous energy restriction on basal and postprandial metabolism: a randomised study in normal-weight, young participants
authors: Yangfan Gao, Kostas Tsintzas, Ian A. Macdonald, Sally M. Cordon, Moira A. Taylor
abstract: This study compared intermittent (5:2) and continuous energy restriction in young, normal-weight individuals. Both diets resulted in similar weight loss, but 5:2 IER improved fasting blood glucose and appetite scores more than continuous restriction.

title: Time-Restricted Eating Without Exercise Enhances Anaerobic Power and Reduces Body Weight: A Randomized Crossover Trial in Untrained Adults
authors: Zifu Yu, Takeshi Ueda
abstract: This study investigated early and delayed time-restricted eating (TRE) in untrained adults. Both TRE methods reduced body weight and improved anaerobic power, with eTRE showing greater weight loss and dTRE greater anaerobic gains.
